cards.text: One of the seven angels with the seven bowls comes to John, the one seeing this vision (Revelation 1:9). The angel says, "Come, I will show you the punishment of the great prostitute, who sits on many waters." Friend, the last time an angel came to talk to me, I was flat on my back under a takeout menu.

cards.question: According to the angel, who was immoral with the great prostitute?
True or false: the angel says the people who dwell on the earth stayed clear of her immorality.

cards.text: Then the angel carries John away in the Spirit into a wilderness, and there's a woman sitting on a scarlet beast. No traffic, no tolls, no parking, friend, just the commute of my DREAMS.

cards.question: True or false: the scarlet beast the woman sits on is covered with names that honor God.
The scarlet beast the woman sits on has ___ heads and ___ horns.

cards.text: The woman is decked out in purple and scarlet, with gold, precious stones and pearls. I spent years in a drawer wearing DUST, friend, and she's wearing a whole jewelry store.

cards.question: The angel said the earth got drunk on the wine of her immorality. Now the woman holds a golden cup in her hand. What is it full of?

cards.text: Then John sees a mysterious name written right on her forehead. Not on a name tag, friend, on her FOREHEAD.

cards.question: Long ago, the prophet Jeremiah spoke to a city that dwells by many waters (Jeremiah 51:13), and this woman sits on many waters too. Which city's name is on her forehead?
True or false: the name on her forehead also calls her the mother of prostitutes and of the abominations of the earth.

cards.text: Then John can see that the woman is drunk, and it's not on wine.

cards.question: What is the woman on the scarlet beast drunk with?

answers.text: the blood of the saints and witnesses for Jesus
the riches of the kings of the whole earth
the praise of the many nations and peoples

cards.text: John has seen a LOT in this vision, and this sight leaves him utterly amazed. I bet his jaw is somewhere down by his sandals.

cards.question: The angel asks John why he is so amazed. Then he offers to tell John the ___ of the woman and the beast that carries her.

cards.text: First, the beast. The angel says it was, and now is no more, but is about to come up out of the Abyss.

cards.question: After the beast comes up out of the Abyss, where does the angel say it goes?

cards.text: Then the angel talks about the people on earth whose names were not written in the Book of Life from the foundation of the world.

cards.question: When the people whose names aren't in the Book of Life see the beast, they will ___.

cards.text: The angel says, "This calls for a mind with wisdom." Friend, when an angel says that, you put the whisk DOWN and lean in.

cards.question: True or false: the angel says the beast's seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman sits.

cards.text: Then the angel adds, "There are also seven kings. Five have fallen, one is, and the other has not yet come."

cards.question: True or false: when the last of those seven kings comes, the angel says he will stay for a long time.
The angel says the beast that was, and now is not, is king number ___ and belongs to the other seven.
The angel says the beast's ten horns are ten kings who haven't received a kingdom yet. How long will they have authority as kings along with the beast?

cards.text: Ten kings, and the angel says they all have one purpose. Friend, the dead batteries I shared that drawer with couldn't agree on ANYTHING.

cards.question: What is the one purpose of those ten kings?

answers.text: to yield their power to the beast
to make the woman their queen

cards.text: Then those ten kings take it a step further and make war against the Lamb, who is Jesus (John 1:29).

cards.question: When the ten kings make war, the ___ triumphs over them.
Why does the Lamb triumph over the ten kings?

answers.text: He rules over all lords and kings
the ten kings turn on each other
the angels fight the battle for Him

cards.question: True or false: the Lamb goes into that war alone.

cards.text: His called and chosen and faithful ones are right there with Him. Friend, THAT is a guest list I'd bake for.

cards.question: The angel goes back to the many waters where the prostitute was sitting. What does he say those waters are?

answers.text: peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues
the seas and rivers of the whole earth
the tears of the saints and witnesses

cards.question: True or false: the angel says the ten horns and the beast will hate the prostitute.

cards.text: They'll leave her desolate and naked, eat her flesh and burn her with fire. The very beast that carried her turns on her.

cards.question: The angel says ___ put it into their hearts to unite and give their kingdom to the beast.

cards.text: I bet those kings think they're running the show. But the angel says they're carrying out God's purpose, until the words of God are fulfilled.

cards.question: Last thing the angel explains is the woman herself. What does he say she is?

answers.text: the great city that rules the kings of the earth
a queen from a land far beyond the sea
an idol the kings of the earth set up

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause, friend, because this story is far from over.

findings.problem: The commute joke comes right after the woman sitting on the scarlet beast. That makes it unclear whose 'commute' it is: John being carried away in the Spirit, or the woman riding the beast. The comparison blurs into the Bible scene, and a stranger could say 'huh?'.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The question says 'the earth got drunk on the wine of her immorality.' Revelation 17:2 says 'those who dwell on the earth were intoxicated,' so the paraphrase changes who is doing it from the people to the earth itself.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the angel's exact word ('mystery') in his line from Revelation 17:7. 'Kingdom' and 'victory' are other possible words the angel could have used. This tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The right answer 'to its destruction' is a fate. Both wrong answers ('to the river Euphrates' and 'to the land of Egypt') are places on a map. Because the right answer is a different kind of thing, it stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'to rebuild the great city' puts the phrase 'the great city' in front of the baker. That phrase is the right answer to stop 2, card 19 ('the great city that rules the kings of the earth'), so this card hints at a later answer.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The core action in Revelation 17:14 is the called, chosen and faithful going with the Lamb into a war. The joke compares them to a party 'guest list,' which is not the same action. It also loosely ties this battle scene to the Marriage Supper without the text making that connection.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells nothing from the passage. It still cites Revelation 17:18, even though the citation rule says a story card cites only the verses it tells.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the continuation line (as the rules allow when the last verse is asked on a choice card), what should its 'verses' field cite? Should it be the last verse of the passage, the verse of the card before it, or something else?
